description: A reverb built on the GVerb code, taking mono or stereo audio and returning stereo, with a CV input and an attenuverter for every control; the maker calls it dirty and unstable

params.text: Sets the size of the modelled room in metres, 2 to 300, which sets the length of the longest delay inside the reverb
Sets how long the tail takes to decay, 0 to 10 seconds
Sets how fast the tail loses its high frequencies, 0 for none and 1 for the most, starting at 0.98
Sets how far apart the two output channels are, mixing them to mono at 0 and leaving them separate at 1; the reverb engine's own spread stays fixed at 90 degrees
Sets how much of the input's high end reaches the reverb, 1 passing the signal whole and 0 filtering it heavily; it starts at 0.01
Sets the level of the early reflections in the reverb signal, 0 to 1
Sets the level of the reverb tail in the reverb signal, 0 to 1
Crossfades the output between the dry input at 0 and the reverb alone at 1
Rebuilds the reverb engine from scratch, clearing whatever it was doing; the knob settings are left alone
Attenuates and inverts the CV going to ROOM SIZE, -1 to +1, and at zero that CV changes nothing
Attenuates and inverts the CV going to DAMP, -1 to +1, and at zero that CV changes nothing
Attenuates and inverts the CV going to TIME, -1 to +1, and at zero that CV changes nothing
Attenuates and inverts the CV going to BANDWIDTH, -1 to +1, and at zero that CV changes nothing
Attenuates and inverts the CV going to EARLY, -1 to +1, and at zero that CV changes nothing
Attenuates and inverts the CV going to LATE, -1 to +1, and at zero that CV changes nothing
Attenuates and inverts the CV going to MIX, -1 to +1, and at zero that CV changes nothing
Attenuates and inverts the CV going to SPREAD, -1 to +1, and at zero that CV changes nothing

inputs.text: The left audio input; a reverb engine for this channel exists only while a cable is patched here, and unpatching the cable throws that engine away
The right audio input; a reverb engine for this channel exists only while a cable is patched here, and unpatching the cable throws that engine away
Modulates the room size; 10V through the ROOM attenuverter at +1 adds 300 metres to the knob setting, and the result is clamped to 2 to 300 metres
Modulates the damping; 10V through the DAMP attenuverter at +1 adds 1 to the knob setting, and the result is clamped to 0 to 1
Modulates the decay; 10V through the TIME attenuverter at +1 adds 10 seconds to the knob setting, and the result is clamped to 0 to 10 seconds
Modulates the input bandwidth; 10V through the BW attenuverter at +1 adds 1 to the knob setting, and the result is clamped to 0 to 1
Modulates the early reflection level; 10V through the EARLY attenuverter at +1 adds 1 to the knob setting, and the result is clamped to 0 to 1
Modulates the tail level; 10V through the LATE attenuverter at +1 adds 1 to the knob setting, and the result is clamped to 0 to 1
Modulates the dry and reverb balance; 10V through the MIX attenuverter at +1 adds 1 to the knob setting, and the result is clamped to 0 to 1
Modulates the channel separation; 10V through the SPREAD attenuverter at +1 adds 1 to the knob setting, and the result is clamped to 0 to 1
A rising edge rebuilds the reverb engine from scratch, clearing whatever it was doing

outputs.text: The left output, crossfading dry against reverb according to MIX; with nothing patched to the left input the dry part comes from the right input
The right output, crossfading dry against reverb according to MIX; with nothing patched to the right input the dry part comes from the left input

notes: an envelope follower inside the module divides both outputs down whenever the reverb climbs past 10V, which can pull the level about on its own during loud passages
the reverb engine is built when a cable is patched to an audio input and thrown away when that cable is removed; with nothing patched to either input both outputs are held at 0V
shift-dragging up or down on the module name changes the colour of the panel, and holding ctrl as well makes the change finer
